Text: Every Java enum type implicitly extends the class {{c1::java.lang.Enum}}, which is why an enum cannot extend any other class.
Extra: Java only supports single class inheritance, and since every enum already inherits from `java.lang.Enum`, they cannot have another parent class.

Text: Unlike standard classes, nested enums are implicitly {{c1::static}}, meaning they do not hold a reference to an outer class instance.
Extra: You do not need to (and cannot) declare nested enums with the `static` modifier manually; it is implicitly done by the compiler.

Text: Java enum constructors must be {{c1::private}}, and trying to declare them as public or protected results in a compile-time error.
Extra: Since enums have a fixed set of constants initialized at class-load time, instantiation via `new` from outside is forbidden.

Text: To maintain the immutability of enum constants, it is highly recommended to declare all enum instance fields as {{c1::final}}.
Extra: Mutable instance fields on enum constants can lead to dangerous race conditions and global state contamination since enum constants are JVM-level singletons.

Text: When an enum defines an {{c1::abstract}} method, each individual enum constant must implement that method in its own constant-specific class body.
Extra: This acts as a clean alternative to switch statements for constant-specific behavior, leveraging polymorphism instead.

Text: The compiler-generated static method {{c1::values()}} returns a cloned array copy of all constants, which can cause GC overhead in hot loops.
Extra: Because arrays are mutable, the JVM clones the array on every call to prevent users from modifying the internal enum constants array.

Text: The static method {{c1::valueOf(String name)}} is case-sensitive and throws an {{c2::IllegalArgumentException}} if no constant matches the given string.
Extra: For example, `Season.valueOf("spring")` will throw an exception if the constant is declared as `SPRING`. It also throws `NullPointerException` if the input is null.

Text: The {{c1::ordinal()}} method returns the zero-based declaration index of an enum constant, which should never be used for database serialization.
Extra: If you insert or reorder enum constants, their ordinal indexes will change, causing existing records in database to point to incorrect states.

Text: Unlike `toString()`, the {{c1::name()}} method is declared {{c2::final}} in `java.lang.Enum`, guaranteeing it always returns the exact declared identifier.
Extra: This makes `name()` the safest choice for serialization and database persistence where a predictable, non-overridable string is needed.

Text: When using an enum inside a switch statement, the case labels must be the {{c1::unqualified}} name of the constant.
Extra: For example, use `case RED:` instead of `case Color.RED:`. Also, if the selector enum variable is null, a `NullPointerException` is thrown.

Text: Although enums cannot extend other classes, they can implement {{c1::interfaces}}, which allows them to participate in polymorphic operations.
Extra: Enums can implement interfaces by implementing the methods at the enum class level or by having each constant override the methods individually.

Text: A single-element enum is the recommended way to implement a Singleton because the JVM prevents duplicate instances during {{c1::serialization}} and blocks reflection instantiation.
Extra: Calling `Constructor.newInstance()` on an enum type throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. Java serialization handles enums uniquely by transmitting only the constant name.

Text: Java serialization prevents duplicate instances of an enum Singleton by writing only the constant {{c1::name}} to the stream, rather than the object data.
Extra: During deserialization, the JVM uses the name to look up the existing instance using `Enum.valueOf()`, ensuring no duplicate instances are created in memory.

Text: When an enum constant has a constant-specific class body, the compiler generates a separate {{c1::anonymous subclass}} for that specific constant at compile time.
Extra: For example, if `Season.SPRING` has a class body, it is compiled as `Season$1.class` extending the base enum class.
